title: Tests need Git Bash's usr/bin tools and the symlink privilege, so tests.py and stress_test.py fail for a standard user outside Git Bash
goal: The test suite passes as a standard (non-administrator) Windows user run from PowerShell or cmd, where Git for Windows puts only Git\cmd on PATH (no sh, test or other usr/bin tools) and creating a symbolic link needs a privilege the user lacks: tests that use POSIX commands as item checks or shims (test_backlog's test -f checks, test_bug_repro_must_fail_now, TestDoneLane, test_benchmarks' shims) use Python commands or skip with a reason when sh is absent, and test_stress's symlink mutations skip when os.symlink raises WinError 1314. Found by TK-vrvthtny's run on a temporary clean local account: tests.py 7 failed, stress_test.py 2 failed, where the operator's Git Bash session (usr/bin on PATH, elevated) passes both. The repro strips usr/bin from PATH; the symlink half is proven by a test that plants WinError 1314.

run: import os,subprocess,sys; env=dict(os.environ); env['PATH']=os.pathsep.join(p for p in env['PATH'].split(os.pathsep) if 'usr' not in p.replace(chr(92),'/').lower().split('/')); sys.exit(subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/tests.py','-k','test_bug_repro_must_fail_now or test_done_refuses_failing_check_and_scope_then_passes or test_the_shims_are_executable_scripts'],env=env).returncode)
